name: Blog posts, long essays
description: Long-form essays numbered in roman numerals, with large titles, a drop-cap excerpt, reading time and hairline rules.

fields.name: intro
fields.label: Intro
fields.default: A few times a year, someone at Marlowe & Finch Architects sits down and writes at length. No project news, just the arguments we keep having at the drawing table.

itemFields.name: title
itemFields.label: Title
itemFields.default: An argument worth a long read

itemFields.name: excerpt
itemFields.label: Excerpt
itemFields.default: Three or four sentences that set out the question the essay asks and why it matters to the people who will read it.

default.title: The case for the boring roof
default.excerpt: A pitched roof with a generous overhang has kept rain out of northern houses for eight hundred years. We spent a decade drawing flat ones anyway. This is an account of four leaks, two awkward client meetings, and what we now sketch first.
default.author: Ingrid Marlowe

default.title: What a staircase teaches you about a client
default.excerpt: Ask someone how they want to arrive upstairs and you learn whether they hurry, whether they carry laundry, and who they expect to meet on the landing. Notes from thirty first meetings.
default.author: Daniel Finch

default.title: Reuse is a drawing problem
default.excerpt: Salvaged brick arrives in mixed sizes and salvaged beams arrive with a history. The hard part is not finding the material. It is drawing a building loose enough to accept it.
default.author: Asha Venkataraman
